s521.content:
Robert Southwell was an English Jesuit who returned secretly to England to serve persecuted Catholics. He was also a fine poet; his Christmas poem The Burning Babe is still anthologized.

Betrayed and arrested in 1592, he was tortured many times and hanged at Tyburn in 1595. He was canonized in 1970 among the Forty Martyrs of England and Wales.
s521.intercession: St. Robert Southwell, pray for us. Make us faithful witnesses to Christ. Amen.

s522.content:
John Ogilvie was raised a Calvinist in Scotland and became a Catholic while studying on the Continent. He joined the Jesuits and returned to Scotland in disguise to minister to Catholics.

Arrested in Glasgow, he refused to acknowledge the king’s authority over the Church and was hanged in 1615. He was canonized in 1976, the only canonized martyr of post-Reformation Scotland.
s522.intercession: St. John Ogilvie, pray for us. Bless the people of Scotland. Amen.

s523.content:
Felix was a farm laborer who became a Capuchin lay brother and spent forty years begging bread for his friary in the streets of Rome. He greeted everyone with "Deo gratias," "thanks be to God," and was nicknamed Brother Deo Gratias.

He was a friend of St. Philip Neri and was the first Capuchin to be canonized.
s523.intercession: St. Felix, pray for us. Teach us to give thanks to God in all things. Amen.

s524.content:
Paschal was a shepherd boy in Aragon who taught himself to read so he could pray the Little Office of the Virgin Mary. He became a Franciscan lay brother, serving as porter and cook.

He spent every spare moment adoring Christ in the Blessed Sacrament. Pope Leo XIII named him patron of Eucharistic congresses and associations.
s524.intercession: St. Paschal Baylon, pray for us. Draw us to adore Christ in the Eucharist. Amen.

s525.content:
Didacus, or Diego, was a Franciscan lay brother from Andalusia who served as a missionary in the Canary Islands. During the Jubilee of 1450 in Rome, he nursed hundreds of sick pilgrims during an epidemic.

He spent his last years at Alcalá in Spain, devoted to prayer and the poor. The city of San Diego in California is named after him.
s525.intercession: St. Didacus, pray for us. Make us generous in caring for the sick. Amen.

s526.content:
Catherine was married young to a careless husband and lived an unhappy, empty life until a sudden conversion in 1473 filled her with the love of God.

She devoted herself to the sick in the great hospital of Genoa, later directing it, and her husband converted and served with her. Her Treatise on Purgatory describes purgatory as the joyful, painful purification of a soul by God’s love.
s526.intercession: St. Catherine of Genoa, pray for us. Purify our hearts with the fire of God’s love. Amen.

s527.content:
Catherine was a Dominican nun and later prioress at Prato in Tuscany. For twelve years she experienced the Passion of Christ in ecstasy every week, from Thursday noon to Friday afternoon.

She was also a capable leader and counselor, corresponding with cardinals, princes, and St. Philip Neri.
s527.intercession: St. Catherine de’ Ricci, pray for us. Help us to share in the sufferings of Christ with love. Amen.

s528.content:
Mary Magdalene de’ Pazzi was a Carmelite nun in Florence whose mystical experiences were recorded by her sisters as she spoke them aloud in ecstasy.

She also endured years of spiritual darkness and illness, and her motto was "to suffer and not to die." She called for the renewal of the Church in letters to the pope and cardinals.
s528.intercession: St. Mary Magdalene de’ Pazzi, pray for us. Kindle in us the love of God. Amen.

s529.content:
Veronica was a Capuchin Poor Clare and later abbess in Città di Castello in Umbria. She received the stigmata in 1697.

At the command of her confessors she kept a spiritual diary of more than twenty thousand pages, a record of her union with the suffering Christ. She was also a practical and kind abbess.
s529.intercession: St. Veronica, pray for us. Unite our sufferings with those of Christ. Amen.

s530.content:
Germaine was a sickly girl from Pibrac near Toulouse, with a deformed hand. Her stepmother treated her cruelly and made her sleep in the stable and tend the sheep.

She went to Mass every day, taught the village children their prayers, and shared her scraps of bread with the poor. According to tradition, when her stepmother accused her of stealing bread, her apron was found full of flowers. Her body was found incorrupt in 1644, and she was canonized in 1867.
s530.intercession: St. Germaine, pray for us. Comfort those who are abused and neglected. Amen.

s531.content:
John Eudes was a French priest and missionary who preached more than a hundred parish missions. He founded the Congregation of Jesus and Mary (the Eudists) to form good priests, and the Sisters of Our Lady of Charity to help women in difficulty.

He wrote the first liturgical texts for feasts of the Sacred Heart of Jesus and the Immaculate Heart of Mary.
s531.intercession: St. John Eudes, pray for us. Make our hearts like the Hearts of Jesus and Mary. Amen.

s532.content:
Anthony was a physician of Cremona who became a priest to heal souls as well as bodies. He founded the Barnabites, the Angelic Sisters, and an association of lay people to renew the Church in Milan.

He promoted devotion to the Eucharist, including the Forty Hours of adoration, and to the letters of St. Paul. He died at thirty-six.
s532.intercession: St. Anthony Mary Zaccaria, pray for us. Bless physicians and all who heal. Amen.

s533.content:
Francis Solanus was an Andalusian Franciscan who sailed to South America in 1589 and preached to the native peoples of what is now Argentina, Paraguay, and Peru.

He learned their languages, and he often played the violin to draw people to hear the Gospel. He spent his last years in Lima, where he died in 1610.
s533.intercession: St. Francis Solanus, pray for us. Bless missionaries and musicians. Amen.

s534.content:
John Macías was a Spanish orphan and shepherd who sailed to South America and became a Dominican lay brother in Lima, serving as porter of the friary.

He fed and cared for the city’s poor and was a close friend of St. Martin de Porres. He prayed the rosary constantly for the souls in purgatory.
s534.intercession: St. John Macías, pray for us. Make us friends of the poor. Amen.

s535.content:
Louis Bertrand was a Dominican of Valencia who served as a missionary in what is now Colombia and the Caribbean from 1562 to 1569, baptizing many and defending the native peoples.

According to tradition, he survived an attempt to poison him. He returned to Spain as a spiritual director, counseling among others St. Teresa of Ávila. He is the patron of Colombia.
s535.intercession: St. Louis Bertrand, pray for us. Bless the Church in Colombia and Latin America. Amen.

s536.content:
Marguerite left France in 1653 for the tiny settlement of Ville-Marie, now Montreal. She opened its first school in a stone stable and taught the children of settlers and of the First Nations.

She founded the Congregation of Notre-Dame, one of the first uncloistered communities of women in the Church, whose sisters taught throughout New France. She was canonized in 1982, the first woman saint of Canada.
s536.intercession: St. Marguerite Bourgeoys, pray for us. Bless all teachers and the people of Canada. Amen.

s537.content:
Laura Montoya was a Colombian teacher who felt called to bring the Gospel to the indigenous peoples of the jungles and mountains, who were often despised and neglected.

In 1914 she founded the Missionaries of Mary Immaculate and St. Catherine of Siena to live among them with respect and love. Canonized in 2013, she was the first saint of Colombia.
s537.intercession: St. Laura Montoya, pray for us. Teach us to respect and love every people. Amen.

s538.content:
María Antonia de Paz y Figueroa, called Mama Antula, was a consecrated laywoman of Argentina. When the Jesuits were expelled from Spanish America in 1767, she kept their Spiritual Exercises alive, organizing retreats for tens of thousands of people.

She walked barefoot thousands of miles across the country and founded a House of Spiritual Exercises in Buenos Aires. Pope Francis canonized her in 2024, the first woman saint of Argentina.
s538.intercession: St. Mama Antula, pray for us. Lead many to meet God in prayer. Amen.

s539.content:
Known as "Cura Brochero," the gaucho priest, José Gabriel Brochero rode his mule across the mountains of Córdoba in Argentina to reach the poor in remote villages.

He built roads, schools, and a great retreat house, and led his people on long journeys to make the Spiritual Exercises. He caught leprosy by visiting the sick, went blind, and died in 1914. He was canonized in 2016.
s539.intercession: St. José Gabriel Brochero, pray for us. Make priests close to their people. Amen.

s540.content:
Narcisa de Jesús Martillo Morán was an orphaned young woman of Ecuador who lived as a laywoman devoted to prayer and penance, supporting herself as a seamstress.

She moved to Guayaquil and later to Lima, where she lived in a Dominican house and died in 1869. She was canonized in 2008.
s540.intercession: St. Narcisa, pray for us. Help us to seek God in prayer and simple work. Amen.

s541.content:
Pedro was a shepherd from Tenerife in the Canary Islands who sailed to Guatemala, where he failed at his studies for the priesthood and became a Franciscan tertiary.

"Hermano Pedro" opened a hospital, a school, and a shelter for the poor, and founded the Bethlemite Brothers. He was canonized in 2002, the first saint of Central America.
s541.intercession: St. Pedro, pray for us. Make us servants of the poor and the sick. Amen.

s542.content:
Toribio Romo was a young Mexican priest during the persecution of the Cristero War. He continued to celebrate the sacraments in secret.

He was shot by government soldiers in 1928. Canonized in 2000 among the martyrs of the Cristero War, he is widely loved as a patron of migrants, and many tell stories of his help on their journeys.
s542.intercession: St. Toribio Romo, pray for us. Protect migrants and all who travel far from home. Amen.

s543.content:
Miguel Pro was a Mexican Jesuit who returned to his country in 1926 when the government had outlawed public worship. Using disguises, he celebrated Mass and brought the sacraments to Catholics in secret.

Falsely accused in a plot, he was executed by firing squad in Mexico City in 1927 without a trial. He forgave his executioners, stretched out his arms like a cross, and cried, "¡Viva Cristo Rey!" Long live Christ the King! He was beatified in 1988.
s543.intercession: Blessed Miguel Pro, pray for us. Give us joy and courage in the service of Christ the King. Amen.

s544.content:
Rutilio Grande was a Salvadoran Jesuit who served the poor rural parish of Aguilares and defended the rights of the peasants.

In March 1977 he was shot on his way to Mass, together with an elderly man and a teenage boy. His death moved his friend St. Óscar Romero to speak out boldly for the poor. He was beatified in 2022.
s544.intercession: Blessed Rutilio, pray for us. Make us defenders of the poor. Amen.

s545.content:
Bernard Casey, a farm boy from Wisconsin, struggled so much with his studies that he was ordained a "simplex" priest, not permitted to preach or hear confessions. As Father Solanus, he served for decades as porter of the Capuchin friary in Detroit.

Thousands came to him for counsel and prayer, and many healings were reported. He often told people to "thank God ahead of time." He was beatified in 2017.
s545.intercession: Blessed Solanus, pray for us. Teach us to thank God ahead of time. Amen.

s546.content:
Stanley Rother was a farmer’s son from Oklahoma who served for thirteen years as a missionary priest in Santiago Atitlán, Guatemala, among the Tz’utujil Maya people, whose language he learned.

During the civil war, when his name appeared on a death list, he returned to his people, saying that a shepherd cannot run. He was murdered in his rectory in 1981 and beatified in 2017, the first martyr born in the United States.
s546.intercession: Blessed Stanley, pray for us. Make us faithful shepherds who do not run. Amen.

s547.content:
Michael McGivney was a young parish priest in New Haven, Connecticut, serving poor Irish immigrant families. Many were left destitute when a father died.

In 1882 he founded the Knights of Columbus, a fraternal society to strengthen Catholic men in their faith and provide for widows and orphans. He died at thirty-eight and was beatified in 2020.
s547.intercession: Blessed Michael McGivney, pray for us. Bless fathers and families. Amen.

s548.content:
Chiara was a cheerful, sporty Italian girl, a member of the Focolare movement. At seventeen she was diagnosed with a painful bone cancer.

She offered her suffering to Jesus with joy, refused morphine so as to stay lucid, and comforted those who came to visit her. She was nicknamed "Chiara Luce," Light. She died at eighteen and was beatified in 2010.
s548.intercession: Blessed Chiara Luce, pray for us. Help the young to find joy in Jesus even in suffering. Amen.

s549.content:
Franz Jägerstätter was an Austrian farmer, husband, and father of three daughters. After the Nazi annexation of Austria, he refused to fight in Hitler’s army, convinced that it was an unjust war.

Despite pressure from neighbors and even priests, he followed his conscience. He was beheaded in Brandenburg on August 9, 1943, and was beatified in 2007.
s549.intercession: Blessed Franz, pray for us. Give us courage to follow a well-formed conscience. Amen.

s550.content:
Karl became the last Emperor of Austria and King of Hungary in 1916, in the middle of the First World War. He worked sincerely for peace and tried to relieve the suffering of his people.

After the war he was exiled, and he died in poverty on the island of Madeira at thirty-four, leaving seven children and his wife Zita, who was expecting their eighth. He was beatified in 2004.
s550.intercession: Blessed Karl, pray for us. Bless all who govern, and grant peace to the nations. Amen.

s551.content:
Jerzy Popiełuszko was a Warsaw priest who became chaplain to the Solidarity labor movement. His monthly "Masses for the Homeland" drew huge crowds; he urged them to overcome evil with good.

In October 1984 he was kidnapped and murdered by officers of the communist secret police. Hundreds of thousands attended his funeral. He was beatified in 2010.
s551.intercession: Blessed Jerzy, pray for us. Help us to overcome evil with good. Amen.

s552.content:
Clemens August von Galen was bishop of Münster during the Nazi regime. In the summer of 1941 he preached three famous sermons denouncing the Gestapo and the secret killing of the disabled, which helped push the regime to officially halt its euthanasia program.

Known as "the Lion of Münster," he was made a cardinal in 1946 and died weeks later. He was beatified in 2005.
s552.intercession: Blessed Clemens, pray for us. Give us courage to defend every human life. Amen.

s553.content:
Rupert Mayer was a Jesuit priest in Munich who lost a leg as a chaplain in the First World War. He became the city’s beloved "apostle of Munich," caring for the poor and preaching tirelessly.

He spoke out against the Nazis from the pulpit and was imprisoned several times, including in a concentration camp. He died in 1945 while preaching a sermon, and was beatified in 1987.
s553.intercession: Blessed Rupert, pray for us. Make us bold in speaking the truth. Amen.

s554.content:
Frédéric Ozanam was a brilliant young scholar in Paris. When a critic challenged Catholic students to show their faith in deeds, he and his friends began visiting the poor in their homes.

In 1833 they founded what became the Society of St. Vincent de Paul, now active around the world. A husband, father, and professor, he died at forty and was beatified in 1997.
s554.intercession: Blessed Frédéric, pray for us. Help us to serve Christ in the poor. Amen.

s555.content:
Anne Catherine was a German Augustinian nun who, after her convent was closed by the state, lived bedridden in poverty, bearing the stigmata and offering her sufferings for others.

The writer Clemens Brentano recorded her visions of the life and Passion of Christ, though scholars note that his books contain much of his own work. She was beatified in 2004 for her heroic virtue.
s555.intercession: Blessed Anne Catherine, pray for us. Help us to love the suffering Christ. Amen.

s556.content:
In 1802 the remains of a young girl were found in the Catacomb of Priscilla in Rome, with tiles reading "Peace be with you, Philomena." They were taken to Mugnano in southern Italy, where many miracles were reported.

St. John Vianney, the Curé of Ars, was devoted to her and credited her with many favors. Little is known of her life, and her feast was removed from the general calendar in 1961, but devotion to her remains widespread.
s556.intercession: St. Philomena, pray for us. Help the young to stay pure and faithful. Amen.

s557.content:
According to an ancient epitaph written by Pope St. Damasus, Tarcisius was a young acolyte carrying the Eucharist to Christians in prison when he was attacked by a pagan mob.

He refused to hand over the sacred Body of Christ and was beaten to death. He is the patron of altar servers and first communicants.
s557.intercession: St. Tarcisius, pray for us. Help us to treasure the Eucharist above all things. Amen.

s558.content:
According to a medieval legend, Ursula was a British princess who was martyred at Cologne with many companion virgins, numbered as eleven thousand, by the Huns.

The legend grew from an ancient inscription in Cologne honoring virgin martyrs. Little can be known for certain, but St. Angela Merici placed her teaching sisters under Ursula’s patronage, and the Ursulines bear her name.
s558.intercession: St. Ursula, pray for us. Bless teachers and students. Amen.

s559.content:
According to tradition, Crispin and Crispinian were brothers who preached the Gospel in Soissons in Gaul, supporting themselves as shoemakers and making shoes for the poor without charge. They were martyred under the emperor Maximian.

The Battle of Agincourt was fought on their feast day in 1415, which is why Shakespeare’s Henry V gives his famous "St. Crispin’s Day" speech.
s559.intercession: Sts. Crispin and Crispinian, pray for us. Bless all who work with their hands. Amen.

s560.content:
Eulalia was a girl of about twelve in Mérida, in Roman Spain. During the persecution of Diocletian she presented herself to the governor, rebuked him for persecuting Christians, and refused to sacrifice to the gods.

She was tortured and burned. The Christian poet Prudentius wrote a famous hymn in her honor, and she became one of the most beloved martyrs of Spain.
s560.intercession: St. Eulalia, pray for us. Give the young courage to confess Christ. Amen.
